operator_io_quirks: All identifiers lowercase, no spaces; still double-quote in generated SQL.
Declared types 'character varchar(3)'/'character varchar(4)' (airports.iata/icao) contain 'char' -> String fuzzer, length arg parsed from '(3)'/'(4)'.
airports.x/y are REAL -> Number fuzzer with scale 0 (no args), so fresh draws are integers in [-1,1] despite real storage; storage class real contradicts declared REAL semantics.
routes.alid is bigint with 0.7% NULLs and FK to airlines.alid; parent airlines.alid includes -1 (sentinel 'Unknown'), so FK draws can hit -1.
routes.codeshare TEXT is 78% NULL, distinct=1 ('Y'); String fuzzer will produce many non-'Y' strings and NULLs.
airlines.iata has '' and '-' sentinels; icao has 'N/A' and NULLs; String fuzzer will not reproduce these sentinels.
airports.name is NOT NULL; upstream does not enforce NOT NULL in Python, so some rows will fail insert and be skipped (writedb behaviour).
airports.iata distinct 5655 < 7184 rows -> duplicates exist; icao distinct = 7184 (unique in practice but not declared unique).
routes has two FKs to airports.apid (src_apid, dst_apid); process_order must handle two child->parent edges to same parent.
airlines.alid includes negative -1; Number fuzzer range [-1,1] for scale 0 will rarely hit -1 but can.
No composite PKs, no self-FKs, no dangling FKs, no views/triggers in DDL.
Table sizes: routes 67240, airports 7184, airlines 6162 — all under 300k, full read fine.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on rid/apid/alid/elevation: scale 0 -> fresh draws in [-1,1] plus +-1/+-2 perturbations; PK rid will collide heavily, sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicates -> tiny routes table.
Number fuzzer on x/y (REAL, no args): scale 0, so fresh values are integers in [-1,1]; original real values only enter via 5 sampled originals + literal pool.
String fuzzer on name/city/country/iata/icao/airline/codeshare: random CHARSET strings length 0..20 (or 0..3/0..4 for varchar args), plus contaminate; will not look like airport names.
String fuzzer on codeshare: 78% NULL originals -> many NULLs; distinct=1 means literal pool tiny; fresh strings dominate.
FK fill: routes.src_apid/dst_apid draw from airports.apid final values; routes.alid from airlines.alid final values (including -1 if sampled).

airports.name NOT NULL: String fuzzer can emit '' (length 0) which is allowed, but NULL only if original NULLs sampled — none, so NOT NULL rarely violated; still possible via contaminate drop-first on empty.
Known FN driver: x/y fresh integers in [-1,1] make latitude/longitude predicates (e.g. x > 100) trivially false/true, killing queries that filter on real ranges.
Known FN driver: rid PK collisions shrink routes to ~few rows, so joins/aggregations over routes return tiny results.
Known FP driver: codeshare distinct=1 means 'codeshare = Y' vs 'codeshare IS NULL' may both match many rows after fuzzing.
Known FP driver: iata/icao sentinels ('', '-', 'N/A') not reproduced; queries testing those sentinels may flip.
Date/Time/Bool fuzzers not dispatched (no such declared types).
